newsitem.title: JAPAN: NKK to reopen furnace to boost steel output -- paper.
newsitem.headline: NKK to reopen furnace to boost steel output -- paper.

text.p: NKK Corp plans to restart a blast furnace with an annual production capacity of about two million tonnes of crude steel to meet increasing demand for steel in Asia, a Japanese daily said on Wednesday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said NKK would resume operations of the furnace at its Fukuyama plant in Hiroshima, western Japan, where three blast furnaces are currently operating. It did not say when the blast furnace closed.
The Fukuyama plant is NKK's key steel plant, and a total of five blast furnaces were in operation there before 1976, the paper said.
The planned reopening of the furnace, which is expected at the end of 1998, will boost the plant's production capacity to 12 million tonnes a year, the paper said.
It said NKK is likely to invest 20 billion yen in the restart of the furnace.
An NKK spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
The decision to reopen the furnace was prompted by increasing demand for steel in Asia and NKK's improved competitiveness through aggressive restructuring, the paper said.
The weak yen is helping NKK to implement cost-cutting steps which were formulated based on an exchange rate of 100 yen to the dollar, it said.
Steel demand in Asia, excluding Japan, is seen growing at an annual rate of over three percent and the region's total consumption of steel is expected to reach 340 million tonnes by the year 2000.
